newsitem.title: USA: Conn. dessert chef cooks up IPO to sweeten coffers.
newsitem.headline: Conn. dessert chef cooks up IPO to sweeten coffers.

text.p: David Glass, creator of a critically acclaimed line of gourmet chocolate cakes, is eagerly serving up slices of his company to investors.

Desserts by David Glass Inc is offering up to 650,000 shares of common stock at $3 per share, with a minimum subscription of 100 shares. Founder and president Glass, 48, personally mailed out the first circulars on Feb 28.
Glass told Reuters he hopes to raise about $2 million to expand his product line and "promote like crazy."
The offering is only for residents of Connecticut, Massachusetts, New York, New Jersey, California, Washington, Florida, and the District of Columbia.
In an unusual move, the securities offer is being made through the Internet, and publicized on cake box labels.

The shares will not be traded on a stock exchange. Instead, Glass's plan is to expand operations, reinvest the net profits, and fatten up the company's net worth and attractiveness to prospective buyers.
If Desserts by Glass were eventually sold or merged, shareholders could be able to sell their shares at a profit.
The lanky, casually dressed Glass knows he's up against some formidable players in the prepared foods industry.
But he thinks his 14-employee company has built a loyal national following since it grew out of his and wife Virginia's home catering business 14 years ago.
"There's not a lot of gourmet stuff out there," Glass said, seated in his factory-style office in Hartford's historic Colt Firearms Building.
"We're trying to make stuff that's fabulous-tasting -- that's delicious, exciting, and unique to eat."

A native of West Hartford, Glass trained in several Michelin three-star restaurants, including Archestrate (now Lucas-Carton) in Paris. He insists on all-natural ingredients in his products, and even blends his own chocolate, because he can't find the exact mix he wants on the market.
Most of the company's cakes weigh about two pounds and retail for $25-30.

Last year's sales were about $1.1 million, an increase of 15 percent over the previous year, Glass said. About 60 percent of the company's sales are in the New England, New York and New Jersey region, Glass said.
The company's flagship product, The Ultimate Chocolate Truffle Cake, is "considered by many chocolate lovers to be the ultimate dessert," according to The New York Times.

Desserts by Glass sells to both retail (specialty stores and supermarket chains) and food service (hotels, restaurants, airlines) accounts. About five percent of its sales come from its annually published catalogue.
Glass products are also sold in other companies' catalogues, including Starbucks Corp's and Balducci's.
Glass has several expansion ideas in the oven, including increased distribution to major international airlines. Glass cakes can now be found on Northwest Airlines Corp and Air Canada flights.
Glass is also pursuing big U.S. restaurant chain accounts. At present, its products are featured in some Planet Hollywood International Inc special events. Other plans

include selling single cake slices in "beautifully designed packages," Glass said. The company is receiving free advice on this project from Vermont ice cream maker Ben & Jerry's Homemade Inc, Glass said.

Glass is also developing chocolate cake shells, to be filled with mousse and liqueur-flavored whipped creams. Late last year it introduced its latest product, The Ultimate Sophia Loren Luscious Almond Cake.

Glass is modest about his dessert-making talents. "My cooking is 50 times better than my baking," he said. "But everybody loved our truffle cake that we used to make for parties," so he decided to specialize.
((--Hartford newsroom (860) 727-0224))
